messages:
sophia: Morning — async update.
What I did: validated AMS + EU buffers, drained 4 nodes in eu-west-1 for a kernel rollback, confirmed ~95% serving lanes healthy.
Blockers: GPU quota bump for eu-west-1 still pending (AWS ticket #3421), and the spot-fallback template didn't apply for eu-west-1b during the drain.
Today: running a small canary of the new runtime on 8 GPUs, re-run spot-fallback, coordinating drain window 10:30–11:00 UTC with @alex.

alex: Quick numbers — ~620 GPUs available across fleet, 35 reserved for Dedicated, so effective EU headroom is ~60 GPUs right now. I can pause non-critical batch jobs during the canary to free ~12 extra GPUs.
I added myself to ticket #3421, will ping infra-ops and cloud-sd.

mona: FYI I saw an eviction spike in eu-west-1b at 03:12 UTC — dumped the short logs to S3: s3://redwood-ops/evictions/1764325000/part-1.log. Looks like a zone-wide preemption wave, not instance-level. I can spin smaller fallback instances if we need quick capacity.

james: Reviewed the canary PR — overall LGTM. One request: bump graceful-kill timeout in the autoscaler from 30s -> 60s to avoid mid-request drops during node reboots. Also adding a tiny metric to track KV-cache miss rate during canary.

rachel: Deploy-bot flagged a node-image-1.2.3 healthcheck failure during the earlier drain (kubelet crashloop). I'm redeploying the image to that pool and will monitor events. Expecting a +10m timeline.

infra-bot: [AUTO] Spot eviction alert: eu-west-1b — 9 instances reclaimed between 03:10–03:20 UTC. Related incident: /incidents/1764325000.

sophia: Thanks — action items: (1) @alex escalate AWS quota (#3421) and confirm ETA, (2) @james update PR with graceful-kill=60s + push metric, (3) @rachel confirm node-image health by 11:15 UTC, (4) @mona prepare fallback small instances ready-to-launch. I'll kick off canary at 11:00 UTC and post perf / tail latency here. :eyes:
